newsitem.title: USA: Micron Elec up on renewed Compaq rumors.
newsitem.headline: Micron Elec up on renewed Compaq rumors.

text.p: Shares of Micron Electronics Inc jumped Thursday on renewed rumors that the direct developer and marketer of personal computers may be acquired by Compaq Computer Corp, traders and analysts said.
Late Wednesday, the online version of Computer Reseller News reported that Compaq is attempting to finalize a deal to acquire Micron Electronics, citing sources close to Compaq.

At Compaq's annual meeting in Houston Thursday, CEO Eckhard Pfeiffer declined to comment when asked about its recent talks with Micron. Two weeks ago, Micron issued a statement saying it had held preliminary talks with Compaq.

Micron and Micron Technology Inc, which owns 64 percent of Micron, said they had had preliminary discussions with Compaq regarding the potential acquisition of Micron Electronics by Compaq. But the companies said at the time that they were not currently engaged in any active discussions, and no offer had been received from Compaq.

Micron was trading up 1-11/16 to 20-1/2. A spokesman for Micron Electronics said that as a policy, it does not comment on rumors and speculation. Traders said the renewed Compaq rumor was driving up Micron's stock, in addition to improved sentiment for PC stocks after IBM Corp's strong Q1.

Analysts said that while they are not surprised that the rumor is resurfacing again, they do not think such a deal would necessarily be the best use of Compaq's big cash pile, which reached $4.7 billion at the end of the first quarter.
"I just don't think it makes any sense and they are not buying a really strong brand," said Louis Mazzucchelli, a Gerard Klauer Mattison analyst. "But you can never say never."
Analysts said that Compaq has been looking at buying a direct developer of PCs as part of its plans to embrace a build-to-order manufacturing strategy.
